p: Constitutionalism means government power is limited by constitutional rules; the Supreme Court said majoritarianism cannot trump constitutionalism.
Foundations: Articles 13, 32 and 226 (judicial review) and Article 50 (separating judiciary from executive in public services).

Key cases: Kesavananda Bharati (1973, Article 368 cannot alter the basic structure), I.R. Coelho (2007, control over governmental power), Puttaswamy (2017, privacy under Article 21), Navtej Johar (decriminalised homosexuality).

A public-spirited person may petition for those who can't approach court; the petitioner can be a third party and letters can be treated as petitions (epistolary jurisdiction). The term was first used in India by Justices Krishna Iyer and Bhagwati.
Landmarks: Hussainara Khatoon (1979, first recorded PIL, under-trial prisoners), M.C. Mehta (1987, Ganga industries), Vishaka (1997, guidelines that led to the POSH Act 2013).

Misuse: the Supreme Court is burdened with over 3,500 PILs; 'ambush PILs' aim at dismissal to block legitimate litigants; Balwant Singh Chaufal (2010) set directions to keep PIL pure and impose costs on busybodies; the petitioner's bona fides must be tested at the threshold.
PAI measures over 2.6 lakh Gram Panchayats on the Localisation of SDGs, grouping the 17 SDGs into 9 themes; Achiever (A+) is a score of 90 or more.
Results: no Gram Panchayat reached Achiever; about 1.4% Front Runners, 45.72% Performers, 47.6% Aspirants and 5.27% Beginners; PAI 2.0 had 97.30% participation with mandatory Gram Sabha validation.
Context: 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX (Articles 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects.

Article 324 gives the Election Commission control of elections; the CEC is removable only like a Supreme Court judge, other ECs on the CEC's recommendation; Article 329 bars court interference in electoral matters.

Anoop Baranwal (2023) set an interim selection committee of PM, Leader of Opposition and CJI; the 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister, uses a Cabinet Secretary-led search committee for five names (which the committee may bypass) and repealed the 1991 Act.

Earlier proposals: Tarkunde, Goswami and Law Commission (255th) suggested PM-LoP-CJI; 2nd ARC suggested also Speaker, Law Minister and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha. In the US the Senate confirms; Canada uses a House resolution.

Sports is Entry 33 of the State List. The National Sports Board has a Chairperson (5 years or till 70) and two Members (5 years or till 67) appointed on a search-cum-selection committee's advice; CAG audits it.
Tribunal orders are enforceable like civil court decrees; the National Sports Policy 2025 replaced the 2001 policy.

topics.t: Million-plus cities, citizenship rules, disqualification and courts (May)
p: India has 47 million-plus cities (nearly one-third of urban population and 60% of GDP) but city governments control on average only 4 of the 18 functions in the 74th Amendment list; reform: directly elected mayors with fixed tenure and a Mayor-in-Council.

Citizenship (Amendment) Rules 2026: CAA applicants must declare any valid or expired passport of Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh; OCI is now fully online (introduced by the 2005 Act, PIO merged 2015), gives a lifelong multiple-entry visa but no voting or constitutional posts.
Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule, 52nd Amendment 1985): merger needs two-thirds of the legislators; the 91st Amendment removed the one-third split rule; the Speaker decides.

Prison Statistics 2024: occupancy fell from 120.8% to 112.7%; 95.8% prisoners male; 34 women's jails (21 States/UTs have none). Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill 2026 raises strength from 33 to 37 excluding CJI (1956 Act fixed 10; Article 124).

e-Courts Mission (2007, National e-Governance Plan; Department of Justice under the e-Committee); Sikkim has the first paperless judiciary. National Compliance Reduction and Deregulation Task Force (2025, Cabinet Secretary) has 23 priority areas; Phase II (Jan 2026); Tripura completed all.
India is a Major Defense Partner of the US and has signed LEMOA, COMCASA and BECA; TRUST covers AI, semiconductors, quantum, telecom; NISAR is a NASA-ISRO mission.

Strains: a 50% US tariff on some Indian goods in 2025 (reduced after an interim trade pact), Russian crude purchases, S-400 under CAATSA and H-1B limits; India argues for multi-alignment (Quad, BRICS, SCO).

India-Norway is a Green Strategic Partnership and India-Sweden a Strategic Partnership; Norway joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI, launched at EAS 2019). Nordic = Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden (Scandinavia strictly Denmark, Norway, Sweden); all five are Arctic Council members; India is an observer since 2013; Himadri station (2008) at Ny-Alesund; ISRO uses Svalbard.

UAE: seven emirates (Fujairah has no Persian Gulf coast; Tropic of Cancer crosses Abu Dhabi). India-UAE CEPA was negotiated in about 90 days in 2022; trade 101.25 billion dollars in FY26; UAE is the only foreign participant in India's SPR (to 30 million barrels), may store crude at Fujairah; CDAC and G42 plan an 8 Exaflop supercomputer; UPI links with AANI and RuPay with JAYWAN; the UAE hosts 3.5-4 million Indians.

topics.t: India-Italy, New Zealand, Vietnam and EU ties
p: Italy: trade target 20 billion euros by 2029; 2027 as Year of Culture and Tourism; Italy joins the Lothal maritime heritage complex; Italy left the BRI in 2023; issues are caporalato exploitation of Indian farm labourers and Italian arms to Pakistan; IMEC was announced in 2023.

India-New Zealand FTA: New Zealand removes duties on all Indian exports and commits 20 billion dollars over 15 years; India opens about 70% of tariff lines, excluding dairy, sugar and onions; 5,000 temporary employment visas a year.

India-Vietnam: Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, trade target 25 billion dollars by 2030, Vietnam joined IPOI, 13 MoUs (incl. Cham manuscripts). India-EU TTC (Feb 2023) has three working groups.

The NPT Review Conference ended without a consensus document (third in a row) as US and Iran clashed; NPT in force 1970; India is not a party; IAEA set up 1957 (India ratified the Additional Protocol in 2014); CTBT bans all test explosions (India hasn't signed); TPNW in force 2021.

Regional nuclear-free zones: Tlatelolco (Latin America), Pelindaba (Africa), Rarotonga (South Pacific), Bangkok (Southeast Asia); Outer Space Treaty 1967 and Seabed Treaty 1971 limit nuclear weapons in space and on the seabed. India joined MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017), Australia Group (2018); not in the NSG. Nine states have nuclear weapons.
OPEC: Baghdad 1960, Vienna HQ, 11 members after the UAE's exit, India not a member; OPEC+ from 2016. Oil benchmarks: Brent (North Sea), WTI (Cushing, Oklahoma), Dubai/Oman (medium sour, for Asia).
Russia-China: 40+ agreements signed during the Russian President's visit. Thucydides Trap (Graham Allison): rising power threatens to displace a dominant one; Athens-Sparta war started 431 BC.

Freedom of navigation: territorial sea 12 nautical miles, EEZ 200 nm; innocent passage applies to all ships including warships; Hormuz is under transit passage. Iran's proposed Persian Gulf Strait Authority would require transit permits. AIIB launched a 10 billion dollar facility for members hit by the Middle East conflict.

UN peace operations 2025: 58 active missions in 34 countries; India among Global South contributors; a UN funding shortfall of about 2 billion dollars. Global Network Against Food Crises (2016): over 266 million people in 47 countries faced acute food insecurity.

Migration: the Global Compact (2018, non-binding), review forum every four years; World Migration Report 2026: about 304 million people live outside their birth country; India-UAE and India-US are the fifth and sixth largest corridors.

Regions: Falkland Islands (UK, claimed by Argentina, 1982 war); Pratas (Dongsha) Island (Taiwan); Belgorod (Russia). B'nei Menashe: Jewish-identifying community of Manipur and Mizoram, over 240 moved to Israel.

NITI Aayog's 'DPI@2047 for Viksit Bharat' proposes DPI 2.0 for 2025-2035 with eight sector transformations (MSMEs, agriculture, education, health and others); the first cycle focuses on MSME and agriculture with lighthouse pilots in six States and a neutral global-engagement body by 2027.

Impact: DPI added 0.9% to GDP in 2022 (4.2% projected by 2030); 80% bank account penetration in eight years (BIS: 47 years otherwise); DBT saved Rs 3.48 lakh crore; DPI MoUs with 24 countries (Feb 2026).
Building blocks: ABHA, AgriStack (land, crop and scheme data), DigiYatra (face recognition for flying), Account Aggregator, ONDC, DigiLocker, UMANG, DIKSHA, PM GatiShakti.

UPI transactions rose from 2 crore (2016-17) to 24,162 crore (2025-26). The IMF (June 2025) called it the world's largest retail fast payment system; it is about 49% of global real-time payments (ACI Worldwide 2024) and live in over 8 countries.
Variants: UPI Lite (on-device wallet for payments below Rs 1,000), Lite X (offline), UPI One World (PPI wallet for foreigners and NRIs), UPI Cash Point.
Challenge: zero MDR makes the model hard to sustain and a few third-party apps dominate.

MoSPI moved the base from 2011-12 to 2022-23 (10th revision; first IIP base was 1937); items rose from 839 to 1,042; gas, water supply and sewerage and waste management added; electricity now splits renewable and non-renewable.
A chain-linked IIP runs alongside the fixed-base index; series are linked by the geometric mean method; formula is Laspeyres; released monthly with a 28-day lag by the NSO.

IFAD's Country Strategic Opportunities Programme 2026-2033 with India (and a parallel NABARD agreement) emphasises SHGs, FPOs and cooperatives; farm workforce is about 46% against about 18% of GDP; over 85% farmers are small and marginal.

FPOs register under Part IXA of the Companies Act or State cooperative laws; SFAC helps States form them; farmers start in Farmer Interest Groups of 15-20; under the 10,000 FPO scheme up to Rs 18 lakh management support for 3 years; CBBOs link them to markets. NAAS suggests better finance, technology and procurement links.

topics.t: Bank capital adequacy and Startup Fund of Funds 2.0
p: CRAR = (Tier 1 + Tier 2) / risk-weighted assets. RBI minimums are CET1 5.5% and CRAR 9%, stricter than Basel III's 4.5% and 8%; banks may now count quarterly profits in CET1. AT1 is separate from CET1.

Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0: Rs 10,000 crore across the 16th and 17th Finance Commission cycles; SIDBI initial implementing agency; invests only via SEBI Category I and II AIFs; government share in an AIF capped at 50%.

Index of Service Production (base 2024-25, from GST and administrative data, formal sector); LEADS 2025 from DPIIT with a four-tier framework; logistics cost about 8% of GDP; over 60% of freight by road.

FDI: entities with up to 10% Chinese shareholding can use the automatic route; 100% FDI in private insurance (LIC capped at 20%) by the FEMA (Second Amendment) Rules 2026. TEAM initiative (2024-27, Central Sector, under World Bank-backed RAMP; NSIC) takes MSEs to ONDC.

RBI surplus of Rs 2.86 lakh crore for 2025-26 (record). Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool: 1.5 billion dollar capacity, Rs 12,980 crore sovereign guarantee, GIC Re as administrator, covers hull, cargo, P&I and war risk, sovereign guarantee above 100 million dollars.

BHAVYA: 100 plug-and-play parks, Rs 33,660 crore over 2026-27 to 2031-32, equity via NICDIT; minimum land 100 acres (25 acres in hilly and NE States). ECLGS 5.0: 100% guarantee for MSMEs, 90% for others and airlines, NCGTC; airline loans 7 years with 2 years moratorium.

Electronic Gold Receipts (SEBI, SCRA securities; BSE first in 2022; redeemable for physical gold). Knowledge-based economy framework (MoSPI). Oil India's new gas find in Rajasthan's Sanu Formation. Mizoram Ginger Mission (MDoNER); ginger needs warm humid climate.
Third public naval strategy after Freedom to Use the Seas (2007) and Ensuring Secure Seas (2015); it handles 'No War No Peace' and grey-zone threats; the 'Net Security Provider' idea dates to 2015.

Facts: 11,098.81 km coast, 1,389 islands, EEZ above 2 million sq km; 95% of trade by volume and 68% by value goes by sea; 88% of crude imports; 12 major and 217 non-major ports; cables carry over 95% of intercontinental data.
Threats: dark vessels and shadow fleets (AIS off), IUU fishing, piracy, maritime terrorism, hybrid threats via maritime militias.

topics.t: Money laundering and the Directorate of Enforcement
p: ED (1956, Enforcement Unit for FERA 1947; now under the Department of Revenue) enforces FEMA, PMLA 2002 and the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018. FY2025-26: 657 prosecution complaints and about 94% conviction rate; assets attached rose 23-fold (Rs 5,171 crore to Rs 1.19 lakh crore).
Framework: UN Vienna Convention 1988, Palermo Convention 2000, FATF (India a member), FIU-IND (VDA service providers now covered), Benami Transactions Act 2016, Black Money Act 2015.

CDS (created 2019 after the 2001 GoM; K. Subrahmanyam Committee): ex-officio Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs, permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee, Principal Military Adviser to the Raksha Mantri; a new CDS was appointed.
Border: 15,106.7 km with seven countries; CIBMS and BOLD-QIT (BSF, Bangladesh border). SIPRI 2025: India 5th largest spender at 92.1 billion dollars (up 8.9%).

AMCA: 5th-generation stealth fighter by ADA (Mk1 with GE-F414); Divyastra (Agni with MIRV); Vayu Astra-1 loitering munition (100 km, 10 kg warhead); NASM-SR; P17A Nilgiri class (Mahendragiri sixth, CODOG); TARA glide kit (RCI Hyderabad, over 80 km). TATP is an unstable explosive; Captagon (fenetylline and amphetamine); Exercise PRAGATI (12 partners, Umroi).

Circular economy replaces take-make-dispose with reuse, repair, refurbishing and recycling; India makes about 62 million tonnes of waste a year, is the world's third-largest e-waste generator and recycles about 10% of e-waste (global about 22%).

Rules: Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 (four-stream segregation), E-Waste Rules 2022, Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 (no landfill or burning), National Critical Mineral Mission 2025 (recycling), EPR shifting to recycling targets and a unified EPR portal; NITI Aayog has a Circular Economy Cell.

topics.t: Energy schemes: small hydro, coal gasification, mCDR
p: Small Hydro Development Scheme: Rs 2,584.60 crore over 2026-27 to 2030-31 for about 1,500 MW; small hydro is up to 25 MW (MNRE); potential 21,133.61 MW across 7,133 sites; Northern Region 7,978 MW (Himachal 3,460 MW); support Rs 3.6 crore/MW (30%, cap Rs 30 crore) in the North East, Rs 2.4 crore/MW (20%, cap Rs 20 crore) elsewhere.

Coal gasification incentive: Rs 37,500 crore (Ministry of Coal), cap Rs 5,000 crore per project, technology-agnostic, competitive bidding, about 50,000 jobs across 25 projects; builds on the 2021 National Coal Gasification Mission; Indian coal has 30-45% ash.
Marine CDR (mangroves, seagrass, alkalinity enhancement): oceans hold over 50 times the carbon of the atmosphere but monitoring and governance are weak; it complements, not replaces, emission cuts.

topics.t: Big cats, dams and El Nino
p: International Big Cat Alliance (2023, India HQ): seven big cats (lion, tiger, snow leopard, leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma); Saudi Arabia is the 26th member; India gave Rs 150 crore for five years.

Dams: India has the third most large dams; 98.5% owned by States; about 26% over 50 years old; Dam Safety Act 2021 (NCDS apex, NDSA regulator); DRIP Phase I (223 dams, DHARMA app); Phases II-III cover 736 dams with World Bank and AIIB funds; eAabhas for flood forecasting.

ENSO has El Nino, La Nina and neutral phases; El Nino weakens the monsoon (droughts of 2002 and 2009); positive IOD can offset it, negative IOD worsens it; 'Super El Nino' is an informal term; Modoki is central Pacific warming. MoES launched an AI monsoon-advance forecast (IMD, IITM, NCMRWF; weekly, four weeks ahead, 16 States) and a 1 km rainfall forecast for Uttar Pradesh.

SEHAT (ICMR and ICAR) links agriculture with health: biofortified crops, integrated farming, farmer health, NCD prevention, One Health. Petersberg Climate Dialogue (Germany, 2010) 17th edition before COP31; first Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels (Colombia and Netherlands) launched a Science Panel.

MARS (UNEP IMEO, launched at COP27) now covers coal mines and waste; Kanjurmarg landfill (Mumbai) is among top three methane sites. World Bank carbon pricing report: covers 29% of emissions, over 107 billion dollars revenue in 2025; India's CCTS is among the largest ETS after China, EU and Korea.

BIS standards IS 19850:2026 (E22, E25, E27, E30) and IS 18698:2026 (DME-LPG); India reached E20; first geothermal plant at Puga, Ladakh with ONGC (1 MWe pilot; GSI found 381 hot springs, about 10,600 MW potential). Global Forest Goals report: forests shrank over 40 million ha in 2015-2025; forest finance 84 billion dollars against 300 billion needed.

Antarctic sea ice loss is linked to deep ocean heat, stronger westerlies and a feedback loop. Heat dome: high pressure traps hot air. Parametric insurance pays on a trigger such as temperature. Cheetahs (Botswana) released at Kuno; Indian soft-shell turtle satellite-tagged in Kaziranga (Schedule I, CITES I, Endangered); pangolins (Indian Endangered, Chinese Critically Endangered, both Schedule I); Prosopis juliflora (invasive, Mexican native, used for green methanol).

topics.t: Examination system (NEET cancellation) and Radhakrishnan Committee
p: NTA runs NEET-UG, JEE Main and CUET; NEET-UG 2026 was cancelled amid alleged paper leaks. Causes: syndicates, weak oversight, policy instability, technology misuse; effects: lost trust and merit; exam malpractice offends Articles 14 and 16.

K. Radhakrishnan Committee (2024): restructure NTA to run only higher-education entrance exams, with ten specialised verticals and a full-time Director-General; at least 1,000 secure test centres (Kendriya and Navodaya Vidyalayas), hybrid CBT plus paper tests, mobile test centres, DM-led committees and a 'DigiExam' with Aadhaar biometrics.
Primary dropout fell from 4.34% (2014-15) to 0.3% (2024-25); internet in schools 63.5%; computers 64.7%; ramps in 79.1% schools; girls' GER at or above boys'.

Gaps: only about 5% of schools run Grades 1-12; 7% have one teacher; about 50% of secondary public schools lack science labs; 1.19 lakh schools lack electricity; secondary GER 78.7%, higher secondary 58.4%, secondary dropout 11.5%; government school share of enrolment fell to 49.25% (private unaided 38.8%).
Learning: under 55% of Grade 3 children can do basic money or measurement tasks and under 30% of Grade 6 handle fractions (PARAKH 2024).

topics.t: SRS Statistical Report 2024 and demographic transition
p: TFR 1.9 (below 2.1 replacement); CBR 18.3; CDR 6.4; IMR 24 (Kerala lowest, 8); U5MR 28; neonatal deaths about 73% of infant deaths; working-age (15-59) 66.4%; aged 60+ 9.7%; sex ratio at birth 918; female marriage age 23.1; institutional deliveries 95.4%.

SRS is run by the Registrar General under the Home Ministry. Demographic Transition Theory (Warren Thompson 1929, Notestein 1945) describes the move from high to low fertility and mortality; one in five Indians will be 60+ by 2050 (347 million).

EAC-PM wants care treated as social and economic infrastructure: women do about 289 minutes a day of unpaid work against 88 for men (Time Use Survey 2024); unpaid care is worth about 15-17% of GDP; India spends under 1% of GDP on care.
Leave: Maternity Benefit Act 1961 gives 26 weeks (establishments with over 10 workers); central staff get 15 days paternity leave; no private-sector law (Sikkim extended it).

Schemes: Palna (Mission Shakti crèches for ages 6 months-6 years), Atal Vayo Abhyuday and Rashtriya Vayoshri, Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0. Four pillars proposed: financing (Parivar Seva Kosh, Carepreneur Fund), workforce, policy reform and quality standards.

topics.t: Health consumption survey and health news
p: NSO health survey (NSS 80th round, 2025): over 60% of hospitalisations in private hospitals; out-of-pocket Rs 50,508 (private) vs Rs 6,631 (public); government health spend 1.43% of GDP vs 2.5% target; doctor ratio 1:811; one rural PHC per 33,800 people; AMRIT pharmacies (HLL Lifecare) give 50-90% discounts; PM-JAY Rs 5 lakh cover.

JANANI platform (MoHFW) upgrades the RCH portal with ABHA/Aadhaar IDs, QR-based mother-child cards and alerts for high-risk pregnancies, linking U-WIN and POSHAN. World Urban Forum 13 (Baku; UN-Habitat; Baku Call to Action); World Cities Report 2026: 3.4 billion people lack adequate housing.
RTE: Lucknow Public School v UP, neighbourhood schools must admit eligible students immediately; Article 51A(k) (parents' duty) and Article 45 (early childhood care below 6).

Women and Men in India 2025: sex ratio at birth 904 to 917; MMR 254 to 88; literacy gap 14.4 points; worker population ratio 76.6% male and 38.8% female; women are 13.65% of MPs. NCRB 2024: crime rate 418.9; cyber crime up 17.9%; suicide rate 12.2; Maharashtra highest; over-speeding the main road accident cause.
Shaheen Malik (2025, Article 142): forcible acid ingestion victims count as acid attack victims under the RPwD Act 2016; acid sellers should be co-accused.

topics.t: Private players in India's space sector
p: IN-SPACe (2020) is the single-window regulator for private space activity; NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm; ISpA is the industry body; Space Policy 2023 sets roles; FDI: 100% (components), 74% (satellite operations and ground segment), 49% (launch vehicles).

Money: Rs 1,000 crore SIDBI venture fund, Rs 500 crore Technology Adoption Fund, Seed Fund up to Rs 1 crore; space economy 8.4 billion dollars (2023), target 44 billion by 2033; over 400 startups; no comprehensive space law yet.

India's GERD is about 0.65% of GDP; 262 researchers per million; IITs get over 80% of ANRF funding. NITI Aayog urges 2% of GDP in 4-5 years, a 'Vigyan Nidhi' fellowship platform, R&D offices, trust-based administration, technology transfer offices and a National Institute for Science Policy and Governance.
Programmes: ANRF (under DST), National Quantum Mission (four hubs), NM-ICPS (25 hubs), Atal Innovation Mission (2016), RDI scheme, NIDHI, PRAYAS.

topics.t: Science and technology news in brief (May)
p: Atlas swarm (China's CETC) vs Indian swarms (Chanakya, Samadh); swarms are scalable, robust and decentralised. Pathfinder orbital data centre (Pixxel and Sarvam; sun-synchronous dawn-dusk orbit; space acts as a heat sink). V2X: TRAI prefers Cellular-V2X over Wi-Fi DSRC. DRDO scramjet combustor ran over 1,200 s (earlier 700 s).

Mission Drishti (GalaxEye) is the first OptoSAR satellite (optical plus radar, launched on Falcon 9). Venus Orbiter Mission (approved 2024; LVM-3; launch March 2028; Sweden joined). ESA-CAS SMILE (first soft X-ray imager). MAVEN saw the Zwan-Wolf effect at Mars. Alfvenic waves may explain the corona's million-degree heat. Vela Supercluster lies in the Zone of Avoidance. Chandrayaan-3 won the Goddard Astronautics Award 2026.

Cell Broadcast System (C-DOT) sends geo-targeted alerts via SACHET. WHA79: second Global Action Plan on AMR (2026-2036; Quadripartite WHO-FAO-UNEP-WOAH), AMR may cause 39 million deaths by 2050. Hepatitis types B, C chronic; A, E by food or water. PCOS renamed PMOS; hantavirus is rodent-borne; Naegleria fowleri causes always-fatal PAM; Ayush Grid (2018) builds A-HMIS and e-Aushadhi.

The Madhya Pradesh High Court declared the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula complex in Dhar a protected monument under the AMASR Act 1958 with a Hindu temple character, based on 94 sculptures and 150+ Sanskrit inscriptions, quashing the 2003 ASI order and citing Articles 25 and 26; it asked for efforts to return the Saraswati idol from the British Museum.

King Bhoja (1000-1055): contemporary of Rajendra Chola I; wrote Samarangana Sutradhara; founded Bhojpur on the Betwa; built Bhojeshwar temple and the Upper Lake of Bhopal on the Kolans. Paramara temples are Bhumija style (evolved Nagara with Dravida touches, tiered miniature spires) and Panchayatana type.

topics.t: Padma awards, Somnath, copper plates and culture news (May)
p: Padma Awards (1954): not titles under Article 18; government servants ineligible except doctors and scientists; committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary. Somnath: Jyotirlinga at Prabhas Patan; 1026 Ghazni attack; restored by Ahilyabai Holkar; consecrated 1951 by Rajendra Prasad.

Netherlands returned 11th-century Chola Leiden copper plates (Rajendra I seal; taken in 1712 from Nagapattinam; grant of Anaimangalam to a Srivijaya-built Buddhist vihara); earliest copper plate is the Mauryan Sogaura plate. Korean War memorial in Seoul for India's 60 Para Field Ambulance. International Booker 2026 (Yang Shuang-zi); Indian winners Geetanjali Shree (2022) and Banu Mushtaq (2025).

Noida worker protests for wage parity show wages as an ethical issue: dignity of labour (Kant; Article 21), distributive justice (Rawls; Article 39(d)), corporate duty (trusteeship), State duty (Articles 41, 43) and migrant vulnerability.

Problems: fewer than 10,000 labour inspectors for 50 crore workers; about 90% informal; race to the bottom as States compete for FDI; CSR used as cover. Fixes: living wage (Article 43), regionally adjusted national floor wage, portable social security, tripartite forums.

topics.t: Samagra Shiksha, PM POSHAN and RBSK
p: Samagra Shiksha (2018, Education Ministry, Centrally Sponsored): merges SSA, RMSA and teacher education; 60:40 sharing, 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States, 100% for UTs without legislature; extended to 30 September 2026 or the 16th Finance Commission scheme; houses Nipun Bharat and PARAKH.

PM POSHAN (formerly mid-day meal; 1995 programme, 2004 scheme, renamed 2021; 60:40): hot meal also for Balvatika; primary 450 kcal and 12 g protein, upper primary 700 kcal and 20 g protein; Tithi Bhojan, social audits; about 11.8 crore children in 11.2 lakh schools.

RBSK (2013, MoHFW, via NHM): screens ages 0-18 for the 4Ds (Defects at birth, Diseases, Deficiencies, Developmental delays); RBSK 2.0 covers 38 conditions, adds mental health and NCD risks; screening at delivery points, Anganwadis and schools; DEICs give integrated care.
The Naval Anti-ship Missile-Short Range (NASM-SR) has been developed by? DRDO.
It uses a solid booster, a long-burn sustainer, an imaging infra-red seeker and a fibre optic gyroscope INS.
A heat dome: it is a high-pressure system that traps warm air near the surface.
Descending air in it is compressed and heated.
High pressure prevents cloud formation, which traps heat and causes heatwaves and droughts.
The cheetah is the only large carnivore declared extinct in India, in 1952.
Project Cheetah is implemented by the National Tiger Conservation Authority.
The African cheetah is Vulnerable; the Asiatic cheetah is Critically Endangered. Cheetahs do not roar.
Pangolins are the only mammals completely covered with keratin scales.
Two pangolin species occur in India: the Indian and the Chinese pangolin.
The Chinese pangolin is found in Assam and the eastern Himalayas; the Indian pangolin occurs south of the Himalayas except most of the North-East.
Egocentric data: it consists of recordings captured from the perspective of the person doing a task.
Egocentric data: it is useful to train Vision-Language-Action models.
Egocentric data: it raises concerns about surveillance, consent and compensation.
It is collected by head, chest or wrist-mounted cameras.
